newsitem.title: CHINA: China removes parliamentarians accused of graft.
newsitem.headline: China removes parliamentarians accused of graft.

text.p: China has removed two members of its rubber-stamp parliament, the National People's Congress, after they were accused of corruption, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Han Guozhu from the northeastern province of Heilongjiang had his delegate status revoked after he was accused of embezzling 120,000 yuan ($14,000) from his employers and of giving his sister $10,000 out of company funds, Xinhua said.
Mao Xingzhong of central China's Henan province was recalled because of accusations he took a large number of bribes while serving as a local Communist Party official, the official agency said.
It gave no details of any further punishments for the two members of China's parliament, which is due to begin its annual session next month.
Corruption, largely unknown under the authoritarian rule of the late Chairman Mao Zedong, has boomed in China as more than a decade of economic reforms weaken strict social controls.
Beijing has repeatedly launched anti-graft campaigns aimed at clearing out officials who barter their bureaucratic clout for economic gain, but many Chinese say the results have been patchy at best.
